From 3c4ae63073d84abee5d81ce46d86a94e9dae9c89 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Date: Thu, 27 Nov 2025 14:47:02 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] mux: mmio: fix regmap leak on probe failure

The mmio regmap that may be allocated during probe is never freed.

Switch to using the device managed allocator so that the regmap is
released on probe failures (e.g. probe deferral) and on driver unbind.

Fixes: 61de83fd8256 ("mux: mmio: Do not use syscon helper to build regmap")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org	# 6.16
Cc: Andrew Davis <afd@ti.com>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Andrew Davis <afd@ti.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251127134702.1915-1-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/mux/mmio.c b/drivers/mux/mmio.c
index 3409af1ffb80..0611ef28bb69 100644
--- a/drivers/mux/mmio.c
+++ b/drivers/mux/mmio.c
@@ -72,7 +72,7 @@ static int mux_mmio_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 		if (IS_ERR(base))
 			regmap = ERR_PTR(-ENODEV);
 		else
-			regmap = regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg);
+			regmap = devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg);
 		/* Fallback to checking the parent node on "real" errors. */
 		if (IS_ERR(regmap) && regmap != ERR_PTR(-EPROBE_DEFER)) {
 			regmap = dev_get_regmap(dev->parent, NULL);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a regmap leak in the `mux-mmio` driver by replacing a non-managed regmap allocation with a device-managed one.

**Modifications**

- **drivers/mux/mmio.c**:  
  In the `mux_mmio_probe()` function, changed `regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg)` to `devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg)`.

**Relationship**  
The single modification ensures that the regmap resource is automatically freed when the device is detached or when probe fails (e.g., due to probe deferral). This eliminates the leak that previously occurred because the manually allocated regmap was never released.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
regmap = regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg);
Reason:
The driver uses the non-managed `regmap_init_mmio()` to create a regmap. This function allocates memory that must be freed by calling `regmap_exit()`. However, the driver does not call `regmap_exit()` on any error path after this allocation (e.g., probe deferral or failure in subsequent steps), nor does it clean up the regmap on driver unbind. This causes a resource leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
regmap = devm_regmap_init_mmio(dev, base, &mux_mmio_regmap_cfg);
Reason:
Replacing `regmap_init_mmio()` with the device-managed version `devm_regmap_init_mmio()` ensures that the regmap is automatically released when the device is detached (on probe failure or driver unbind). This eliminates the need for explicit cleanup and fixes the leak.
